title: Frequently Asked Questions: Payments
description: Find information about Payments related to car auctions at Bidders Highway.
mainHtml:
FAQschevron_rightPayments

Payments

  • What happens if I don't want to go through with my purchase?

    All bids are binding. You must approve this in order to place a bid. This means that the winning bidder's bid fee will not be refunded even if they withdraw from the purchase. More about this in our general terms and conditions.

    Read more

  • How currencies work

    The currency in which fees are paid is determined by where an item has been accepted for sale. Items shipped within Sweden are valued, sold and paid for in Swedish Kronor (SEK). All additional fees for such items are in Swedish Kronor (SEK). The exchange rate quoted (e.g. Euro €) at the time of the auction is a current estimate and may vary depending on the time of sale.

    Read more

  • What does BUY NOW mean?

    Some of our items are listed under the BUY NOW category. This means that the seller has chosen to list their car at a fixed price that guarantees a sale. These items have no set time limit. By being the first to click on BUY NOW, you can buy the item at the set price.

    Read more

  • Can I withdraw my bid?

    All bids are binding and it is up to you as the bidder to ensure that you feel safe and comfortable placing a bid based on the information available. More about this in our terms and conditions.

    Read more

  • How much does it cost to buy a car on Bidders Highway?

    The price you see when an auction is closed is the price the buyer pays the seller. In addition, the buyer pays a fee of 7.5% (VAT included) of the winning bid to Bidders Highway after the auction is closed. This fee is limited to a maximum of 75,000 SEK and a minimum of 5,000 SEK.

    Read more

  • When will I receive the purchase price if my car is sold at auction?

    Once the auction has ended and there is a bid that meets the reserve price, Bidders Highway will make a digital introduction between you and the bidder with the winning bid so that you can agree on the desired payment method together.

    Read more

  • What happens after the auction ends if my vehicle is sold?

    Once your vehicle has reached the desired reserve price and the auction is closed, Bidders Highway will first contact the buyer to charge the fee. Once this has been paid, we will make a digital introduction between buyer and seller to complete the payment and agree on the handover of the vehicle.

    Read more

  • Can I have a reserve price on my auction?

    Yes, you may set a reserve price on your auction. If the bidding ends at a price lower than the reserve price, the car will not be sold. We are happy to help estimate an approximate price for the car if it's interesting to us, but remember that the market is always in control: The final price of your lot will be determined by what others are willing to pay for it.

    Read more

  • How much does it cost to sell with Bidders Highway?

    For the work done on your auction, we charge a fixed sales fee of SEK 2,995 (incl. VAT) per published auction. The fee includes: professional photography, valuation and advice, copy and layout of the ad, publication on Bidders Highway, exposure in newsletters and social channels, and publication on selected external advertising sites (e.g. mobile.de and Blocket). We also charge a variable fee o...

    Read more

  • Do you offer secure payments between buyer and seller?

    Buyers and sellers on our platform can choose to use Swiftcourt, an external and independent service for secure transactions. Swiftcourt is an escrow service that manages the payment between the parties and keeps the money safe until the transaction is completed. This is a convenient and voluntary support service to facilitate safer transactions between our users.

    Read more

  • What is Secure payment with Swiftcourt (escrow) and how does it work?

    Escrow means a neutral third party (Swiftcourt) safely holds the funds until both parties have fulfilled their obligations. The money is released only after both parties confirm the handover.
